vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: memory-dream
Version: 1.0.0

The 'memory-dream' skill is a utility designed to consolidate an agent's daily logs into a long-term memory file (MEMORY.md). The instructions in SKILL.md and README.md describe a legitimate memory management process with explicit safety rules, such as using surgical edits instead of overwriting, never deleting files, and ensuring secrets/tokens are not included in reports.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions, required actions, and lack of external dependencies are consistent with its stated purpose of consolidating local memory files into MEMORY.md, but it does modify local files so you should review and back up your data before use.

dimensions.detail: Name and description match the runtime instructions: the skill inventories memory/*.md, scans recent daily notes, and surgically updates MEMORY.md. The only minor mismatch is that SKILL.md operates on specific workspace files (memory/ and MEMORY.md) but the package does not declare any required config paths — it assumes the agent has access to the standard OpenClaw workspace.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions explicitly tell the agent to run file operations (ls memory/, read MEMORY.md, read recent memory files, edit MEMORY.md, append a log). Those are within the stated purpose. However the skill will read and write local files that may contain sensitive data (API keys, tokens, private notes) if present — the SKILL.md warns about not exposing secrets in reports but does not provide automated secret-detection or sanitization steps.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only (no install spec, no code files), so nothing will be downloaded or executed during install. The README suggests optional manual installs from GitHub or curl, but those are user-driven and not part of an automated install flow embedded in the skill package.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, no credentials, and no special config paths. That is proportional to its local file-manipulation purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (default) and model invocation is allowed (normal). The key privilege is that the skill is designed to autonomously edit MEMORY.md and append to daily memory files when invoked. This is expected behavior for a consolidation skill, but it means the skill can change your workspace files without additional prompts when invoked (manually or via Cron/Heartbeat).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing:

- Backup your workspace (MEMORY.md and memory/*.md) so you can recover if edits are unexpected.
- Inspect recent daily memory files for any secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords). If found, remove or move them before running the skill — the skill will read those files and could copy sensitive strings into MEMORY.md if not careful.
- Test the skill on a copy of your memory directory first (run it manually, not via cron) to confirm the consolidation behaviour and that the surgical edits meet your expectations.
- Review how your OpenClaw agent's 'edit' tool works and which user account the agent runs as (file permission boundaries). Ensure the agent has only the file access you intend.
- If you plan to follow the README installation instructions that clone or curl from GitHub, inspect that remote repository before running those commands; the packaged skill itself contains no code, but following external install instructions pulls third-party content.
- If you want tighter control, avoid enabling automatic cron/heartbeat triggers until after manual validation, or limit cron to run on a schedule you approve.

Overall this skill is coherent with its stated purpose, but because it reads and mutates local files, exercise the normal operational precautions (backup, review, test) before enabling automatic runs.
